rows.description: A team member who raises a risk is called negative or not a team player. They learn that honesty costs belonging and may go quiet or leave.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: nostalgia

rows.description: A manager notices that discussions end too easily and nobody argues. Instead of relief, they read this as a warning that people are not speaking up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: relief

rows.description: A wise lead asks someone to argue against the plan, speaks last, and thanks the person who raises problems. Making dissent safe and normal protects the group from its own confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: gratitude, trust

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A child sees a classmate fall or get bullied and does nothing because many others are watching too. Each assumes someone else will step in, so nobody does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
possibly related concept (heuristic): Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A child learns that getting help from a teacher or parent is not tattling but caring. They practise saying I need help and pointing at one specific adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A teenager sees something troubling in a group, such as a fight or a drunk friend, and looks around to check whether it is serious. Seeing calm faces, they decide it must be fine.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm
possibly related concept (heuristic): Moral disengagement: displacing and diffusing responsibility

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A teenager hesitates to help because they fear looking foolish if they misread it. Social risk outweighs the victim's need in the moment, and guilt arrives later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, embarrassment, guilt

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A student being harassed notices that many people see it and nobody speaks. The silence of the crowd can hurt more than the act itself and teaches them they are alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hurt

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A teenager chooses a low-risk action such as checking on the victim, distracting the aggressor or calling an adult. Safe helping is a range of options, not a heroic all-or-nothing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hostility, trust

rows.subtopic: Bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility
rows.description: A student sees a cruel or dangerous post in a big group chat and assumes someone else will report it. The bigger the group, the smaller each person's felt duty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger
